formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once the signature is submitted before the deadline, the vault sets the spender's allowance over the owner's ifUSDC vault shares to exactly `value`. The new allowance replaces the old one and does not expire.

The spender can then move up to `value` shares with transferFrom, or use withdraw/redeem to turn them into USDC sent to any receiver. Only type(uint256).max counts as an unlimited allowance that is never spent down.
Submitting the signature uses up the owner's current nonce. No asset moves and no native value is spent when signing.
formats.shown: "Approve <value> ifUSDC for <spender> until <date>", with fields for the share owner, the spender, the allowance amount (in ifUSDC, showing 'Unlimited' at max uint), the signature deadline and the nonce.

findings.title: Permit: the sentence 'Approve X for spender until deadline' suggests the allowance expires, but it does not.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json interpolatedIntent: "Approve {value} for {spender} until {deadline}". ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit: `if (block.timestamp > deadline) revert ERC2612ExpiredSignature(deadline); ... _approve(owner, spender, value);` The deadline only limits when the signature can be submitted. The allowance set by _approve has no expiry. Case 0 renders "Approve 1.5 ifUSDC for 0x5F3b… until 2030-01-01 00:00:00Z".
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Approve {value} for {spender}, signature valid until {deadline}" or "Approve {spender} to spend {value}". The 'Signature deadline' field already shows the date.
